paper_title: Development and validation of a real-time prediction model for acute kidney injury in hospitalized patients
prediction_task: Real-time AKI prediction in hospitalized patients (54-90h before onset), validated across 5 hospitals

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Did authors set threshold for missing data to exclude features with high missingness? Were validation models run on complete-case or imputed data? Several features (procalcitonin, D-dimer, troponin) are not routine — how should model be applied when absent?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added missing data thresholds, complete-case vs imputed comparison, and model behavior with absent lab values.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Among 20 features, 'Use of diuretics', 'Admission to ICU', and 'Use of human albumin' vary between centers and have most significant SHAP contribution. This could limit stability and generalizability.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added center-specific performance analysis and leave-one-center-out validation.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Why were patients with AKI in first 24 hours excluded? These seem like the patients you'd want to identify — many Stage 1 AKI within 24h develop Stage 2/3 over next 24-72h. Why exclude baseline creatinine <0.6 mg/dL — these include older patients and cancer patients at high risk.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added sensitivity analysis including early AKI and low-baseline patients.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Imputing normal values for procalcitonin/troponin when not tested is problematic — if 80% of cohort has imputed normal values, this creates systematic bias. Tests not ordered may indicate clinical judgment that the patient is lower risk.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added missingness indicator variables and analysis of informative missingness.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Almost all 95% CIs of AUC values are either very narrow or similar to mean estimate. Models and AUC estimates obtained through multiple iterative testings may increase likelihood of false positive findings.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Clarified CI calculation method and added bootstrap CIs.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: 5.4% having AKI across total cohort seems low. 40% of AKI in ICU also seems low. How were duplicate patients handled if same patient had AKI during repeat admission?
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added AKI incidence comparison with literature and clarified duplicate patient handling.

reviewer_strengths.text: Commendable for large sample size and substantial number of events in comparison to number of predictors. Multicenter validation affirms predictive validity.
Bringing modern AKI risk prediction to the developing world is an important merit.
